flawed_step: The implication ignores that the proportions of strata C and not-C can differ between T and not-T.
counterexample: Take 200 equally likely individuals. In T∩C, 9 of 10 succeed; in T∩not-C, 18 of 90 succeed; in not-T∩C, 72 of 90 succeed; in not-T∩not-C, 1 of 10 succeeds. Thus within C, 9/10 > 72/90, and within not-C, 18/90 > 1/10. But overall, P(S|T)=27/100 while P(S|not-T)=73/100, so P(S|T)<P(S|not-T). All four strata have positive probability.
assessment_summary: A concrete Simpson's-paradox configuration satisfies both stratum-wise inequalities but reverses the overall inequality.
